keyPhrases.de: Entschuldigung, wie komme ich in die Altstadt?
keyPhrases.text: Excuse me, how do I get to the old town?

keyPhrases.de: Das Haus steht über dem Fluss.
keyPhrases.text: The house is standing over the river.

keyPhrases.de: Könnten Sie bitte ein Foto von uns machen?
keyPhrases.text: Could you please take a photo of us?

keyPhrases.de: Ich hätte gern drei im Weggla, bitte.
keyPhrases.text: I'd like three in a roll („im Weggla“), please.

keyPhrases.de: Nürnberg hat mir sehr gut gefallen.

subtitles.text: We're in Nuremberg! And … where do we go now?
Leo, you're holding the map upside down!
Today we're spending a whole day in the old town – with churches, fountains and the famous bratwurst.
Bratwurst? Count me in!
And everywhere we ask you: What do you say?
And you only have five seconds!
You come out of the station. You want to go to the old town. A woman is waiting next to you at the traffic light.
What do you say?
A: Old town. Where?
B: Excuse me, how do I get to the old town?
C: Excuse me, how do I get to old town? (wrong preposition)
C! Sounds good to me.
Almost, Leo. It's „in die Altstadt“. A is too short and impolite. B is perfect!
Easy: go straight on here, through the gate, and then all the way along Königstraße.
Five minutes!
Thank you very much!
Repeat after me!
Excuse me, how do I get to the old town?
The first church: St. Lorenz. Look up!
Wow! How tall are the towers?
Listen carefully: the towers are over eighty metres tall.
How tall are the towers?
A: over 18 metres
B: over 80 metres
C: over 800 metres
B! Achtzig (eighty) – with „-zig“ at the end. Achtzehn (eighteen) is much smaller.
And the church is very old: it took over 200 years to build.
Repeat after me!
How tall are the towers?
Over 80 metres.
We're standing on the bridge. In front of us: the Holy Spirit Hospital. It used to be a hospital.
Look! The house is standing in the river!
Where is the house?
A: The house is standing in the river.
B: The house is standing on the river. (wrong grammar)
C: The house is standing over the river.
C! There are two arches under the house – and the water flows through underneath.
„In the river“ would be pretty wet!
Repeat after me!
The house is standing over the river.
You want a photo together. A man with a bike helmet walks past.
What do you say?
A: Take photo! Quick!
B: Can you please will photograph me? (wrong grammar)
C: Excuse me, could you please take a photo of us?
C! With „Könnten Sie bitte …?“ (Could you please …?) every request sounds friendly.
A is an order – and B is grammar chaos.
Sure! Smile, please … and one more. There you go!
Great, thank you very much!
Repeat after me!
Could you please take a photo of us?
This is the Schöner Brunnen – the Beautiful Fountain. That's really its name!
Do you see the golden ring in the railing? If you turn it, you can make a wish.
What does Leo do now?
A: He turns the ring and makes a wish.
B: He takes the ring home.
C: He washes his hands in the fountain.
I wish for … a bratwurst!
A! But don't tell anyone your wish – or it won't come true.
Repeat after me!
I'm making a wish.
Opposite is the Church of Our Lady.
At the top there's a special clock: every day at twelve o'clock, little figures walk around the emperor.
What time is it?
Leo looks at his watch: it's a quarter to twelve. How long do they have to wait?
A: a quarter of an hour (15 minutes)
B: an hour
C: four minutes
A! „Viertel vor zwölf“ is 11:45. 15 more minutes until the little men start walking.
Repeat after me!
What time is it?
It's a quarter to twelve.
Finally: bratwurst!
Hello! What can I get you?
What do you say?
A: I am three bratwursts.
B: I'd like three in a roll („im Weggla“), please.
C: Give three bratwurst!
A! I am three bratwursts!
Leo, you're not a bratwurst! B! „Drei im Weggla“ – that's how you say it in Nuremberg: three small bratwursts in a bread roll.
„Weggla“ is Franconian for bread roll.
With mustard?
Yes, with mustard, please.
Repeat after me!
I'd like three in a roll („im Weggla“), please.
Yes, with mustard, please.
And for dessert: Nuremberg gingerbread!
You want to know the price. What do you ask?
A: How much is the gingerbread?
B: How much is the gingerbread old? (wrong)
C: How expensive am I?
A! With „Wie viel kostet …?“ you ask for the price.
One pack costs €4.50.
Say the euros first, then the cents: vier Euro fünfzig – four euros fifty.
Repeat after me!
How much is the gingerbread?
Four euros fifty.
In St. Sebald's Church there is a huge bronze tomb. Look down!
The tomb is standing on … snails?!
What is the tomb standing on?
A: The tomb is standing under snails.
B: The tomb is walking with snails.
C: The tomb is standing on snails.
C! And guess what? The artists worked on it for eleven years.
Maybe the snails were the bosses. That's why it took so long!
How long did it take? Eleven years.
Repeat after me!
How long did it take?
Eleven years.
In the evening we're at the Neptune Fountain. And Leo plays Neptune …
I am the king of the sea!
A friend calls and asks: „How was Nuremberg?“ What do you say?
A: Nuremberg liked me very much. (wrong!)
B: I liked Nuremberg very much.
C: Nuremberg pleases me very much. (wrong case: „mich“)
B! With „gefallen“ the city is the subject: Nürnberg hat mir gefallen.
And „Ich habe Nürnberg gefallen“ means: the city liked you!
Repeat after me!
I liked Nuremberg very much.
Three tips for Nuremberg. First: the old town is small – you can walk everywhere.
Second: during Advent there's the famous Christkindlesmarkt (Christmas market) here.
And third: Nuremberg is in Franconia, in Bavaria. That's why you often hear „Grüß Gott“
instead of „Guten Tag“.
Many people in Nuremberg speak Franconian. And Leo doesn't understand a word …
A Weggla? (Franconian)
A bread roll!
Grüß Gott! (Hello!)
Good day!
Ade! (Bye!)
Bye!
A weng? (Franconian)
A little bit!
Bassd scho! (Franconian)
It's fine – that's okay!
How do I get to old town? (wrong)
„In die Altstadt“! How do I get to the old town?
The house is standing in the river.
Over the river! The house is standing over the river.
„Ich habe Nürnberg gefallen.“ (wrong)
„Nürnberg hat mir gefallen!“ – I liked Nuremberg!
And now everything once more. The ten most important sentences. Repeat after me!
Excuse me, how do I get to the old town?
The towers are over 80 metres tall.
The house is standing over the river.
Could you please take a photo of us?
I'm making a wish.
It's a quarter to twelve.
I'd like three in a roll („im Weggla“), please.
How much is the gingerbread?
How long did it take?
I liked Nuremberg very much.
Which city in Germany should we visit next? Write it in the comments!
Bye – and see you soon at LilyLingua!
